correctness.rationale: Equations (1)–(5) in RESULT.md prove a complete joint weak limit for all fixed positive parameter vectors. Distinct fixed-rank subset overlaps have a strictly higher Dirichlet boundary exponent; cross-rank joint excursions have probability o(1/m) because the larger subset contains a nonempty part disjoint from the smaller one. Scaling exponents strictly separate and make the join concavification inactive with probability approaching one. The standard-library checker passed 809 finite diagnostics, which are not used as proof. All dimension-two and tie cases are included.

value.rationale: Random majorization joins describe the smallest common concentration profile for heterogeneous probability vectors. The theorem determines the full n-1-dimensional simultaneous rare-boundary law, exhibits rank-dependent powers from minimum concentration subsets and tie-count intensities, and establishes asymptotic separation despite within-vector dependence. This is a meaningful complete structural classification of a naturally motivated extremal object, beyond isolated Beta order statistics or generic one-dimensional tail formulae.
